figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of Li-ion self-diffusion study in the metallic Li anode, Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) electrolyte, and supercells with Li/LLZO interfaces. The study includes four stages: (a) initial generation of the training conﬁgurations, using the ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations; (b) training of MLIPs, using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and active learning; (c) large-scale MD simulations with MLIPs; and (d) validation of MTPs.

FIG. 3. Comparison of migration pathways and activation ener- gies obtained with the DFT-NEB and MTP-NEB approaches: [(a) and (b)] bulk t-LLZO and [(c) and (d)] supercell with Li/t-LLZO interface.

FIG. 4. Li-ion diffusion study in both the low-temperature vacancy-mediated regime and the high-temperature Frenkel-defect-mediated regime. The ﬁgure presents the crystal structure, the mean-squared displacement (MSD) as a function of temperature, diffusion coefﬁcients with Arrhenius ﬁts, and the Li-ion probability density map for the low-temperature regime at an isosurface level of 5 × 10−4 r−3 Bohr. The following bulk phases were analyzed: [(a)–(d)] tetragonal LLZO (t-LLZO) without vacancies, [(e)–(h)] Ga-doped LLZO (Ga-LLZO), and [(i)–(l)] body-centered cubic lithium (Li metal). To avoid trajectories with poor statistics, we included only those for which MSD exceeded the squared typical jump length in the bulk phases, that is, MSD > 9 Å2 (dotted lines on plots).

FIG. 5. (a) Self-part [4πr2Gs(r,t)] and (b) distinct part [4πr2Gd(r,t)] of the radial one-dimensional van Hove correlation function for Ga-doped LLZO at T = 700 K, shown for lag times t ranging from 2 to 1000 ps. Circles mark the local maxima (peak positions) for each curve. In the self part, the ﬁrst peak (0 < r ⩽ 1.8 Å) corresponds to ion rattling, the second peak (1.8 < r ⩽4 Å) arises from single-ion jumps, and the third peak (4 < r ⩽6 Å) is attributed to cooperative jump events. In the distinct part, the ﬁrst peak (0 < r ⩽1.5 Å) reﬂects cooperative hopping events, while the second peak (1.5 < r ⩽4 Å) originates from single-ion jumps.
FIG. 6. Ratio of cooperative hops (ηnorm), calculated using Eq. (7), for the considered bulk phases: t-LLZO (without vacancies), t-LLZO (with 1.8% vacancies), c-LLZO, Ga-LLZO, and Li metal.

FIG. 7. (a) Crystal structure of a supercell with Li/Ga-LLZO interface. (b) The mean-squared displacement in the direction perpendicular to the interface plane (MSDZ) as a function of temperature. To avoid trajectories with poor statistics, we included only those for which the MSDZ exceeded the squared half-size of the supercell, that is, MSDZ > 100 Å2 (dotted lines on plots). (c) Exchange-current of Li+ in the z direction as a function of temperature and its Arrhenius ﬁt. Minimal residence time between Li+ jumps across the interface was set to 2.8 ns.
FIG. 8. Activation energy of charge transfer for the Li/Ga-LLZO interface as a function of the minimal residence time tresidence. The converged value is (167 ± 18) meV.
